messages.author: f5653fd64c50597c
messages.subject: plotting to a pdf file
parts:
Hi all,

I've just recently started playing around with ggplot2, and wanted to
write a series of plots to pdf files. Using the example from the
ggplot2 documentation on qplot, I tried:

library(ggplot2); pdf('test.pdf'); qplot(mpg, wt, data=mtcars);
dev.off()

The above works fine (takes ~3 secs to draw then saves the plot), and
writes the correct plot to test.pdf (~12kb). However, if I encase the
command in braces like so:

library(ggplot2); {pdf('test.pdf'); qplot(mpg, wt, data=mtcars);
dev.off()}

R does not spend any time drawing the plot, and saves an empty pdf
file (~4 kb). The reason I need the braces is I'm running a for loop
around the graph generation, but narrowed down the problem to simply
using braces.


Any ideas?

Thanks,

Gerald.

messages.author: 674305bdd88beadd
messages.subject: Re: plotting to a pdf file
parts:
Gerald,

try plotting as usual and then use ggsave, e.g.:

qplot(.... yourarguments ....)
ggsave("yourpath/",scale=1.5)

hth

matt

Gerald,

I agree with Mark. Below is a sample snippet of code I use to produce plot output. I typically keep my plotting scripts as separate files, so I can wrap my pdf plot command around a source command. But I'm a novice, so I'm still learning!
pdf("/yourfile.pdf", onefile = TRUE) # Using onefile = TRUE makes a single, multipage pdf if you have multiple plots.

... # This is where I'd source my .r script for creating plots

dev.off()

- Brian
